newsitem.title: MEXICO: Maseca shares up on price hike report.
newsitem.headline: Maseca shares up on price hike report.

text.p: Shares listed by corn flour and tortilla manufacturer Maseca headed the prominent gainers' list in early trade on the Mexcican Stock Market on a radio report tortilla prices were to increase, traders said.

"The report has been denied by the Mexican Trade Ministry (Secofi), but producers have been exerting considerable pressure to raise prices, and the uncertainty could lead to considerable speculation," a Mexico City desk trader said.
Maseca B shares gained 22 centavos to 8.24 pesos following the radio report band, then receded to a gain of four centavos.
Mexican radio network Radio Red said the current price ceiling on tortillas of 1.70 pesos per kilo was to be raised to 2.50 pesos next month.
A Secofi spokesman, however, told Reuters a price hike was "not on the cards."
Tortillas are maize pancakes that have been a staple part of the Mexican diet for many centuries, and are one of the few foodstuffs which are still subject to price controls.
"This is an election year and a price hike that would hit workers would be politically very delicate, so maybe they won't raise prices until after the elections," the trader added.
Elections will be held in July to renew the entire lower house of Congress and one quarter of the Senate, for several state governors and for mayor of Mexico City.
